text:
sam: kicking off an A/B cascade for v4-alpha-int8 -> goal is 4-stage ramp with per-slice weight decay if regressions appear
nina: quick summary of the cascade?
sam: Stage 0: shadow 10% for 90m across uniform; Stage 1: live 0.2% for narrow slices (longform, docs) 60m; Stage 2: 1% live for all longform 60m; Stage 3: 5% live broad 2h. Hysteresis: need 2 consecutive windows passing to advance. single-window fail = halve traffic; 2 fails = rollback.
derek: what defines pass/fail? thresholds please
sam: baseline = prod v3.9-pt. Gate vector: ROUGE-L_delta, exact_match_delta, halluc_rate_delta, latency_p95_delta, embed_sim_drop. Passing condition = at least 4/5 metrics within thresholds AND no slice breach > slice_abort.
product-amy: put a safety multiplier for hallucinations, small increases are worse than ROUGE drops
sam: agreed. we weight halluc_rate x2 in the composite tie-break. final_score = mean_normalized(rouge,exact_match,embed_sim) - 2*halluc_delta - latency_penalty. auto-fallback if final_score < -0.04 OR any slice metric > 0.06.
eval-bot: shadow run complete (90m)
eval-bot: OVERALL: ROUGE-L -0.007, exact_match -0.003, halluc +0.009, latency_p95 +0.05, embed_sim -0.012
nina: overall looks OK but slice check?
eval-bot: SLICES: api_readme longform: halluc +0.041 (40 samples), kb_exports short: embed_sim -0.065 (25 samples)
derek: api_readme > slice_abort. we should bisect to isolate code path. could be input normalization or kv-cache dropout with int8.
sam: plan: run targeted shadow where we route only api_readme and vary model variant weights: native-pt only, int8-only, ensemble mix 0.8/0.2, 0.6/0.4. collect 500 samples each.
eval-bot: targeted shadow runs queued
eval-bot: results: pt-only: halluc +0.003, int8-only: halluc +0.047, 0.8/0.2: +0.018, 0.6/0.4: +0.031
nina: clearly int8 is the offender on that slice
derek: can we do adaptive-slice-weighting instead of full rollback? reduce int8 weight for api_readme to 0.05 and let pt dominate for that slice, keep higher int8 elsewhere
sam: yes our routing supports per-slice weights. I'll propose a policy: per-slice variant cap = 0.2 default, reduce by half on first slice breach, floor at 0.05.
product-amy: need to reflect that in incident timeline and console events for product metric owners
ops-sre: add hard p95 latency ceiling of +0.2 relative; if exceeded, immediate cut to 0% and pager to oncall. Also emit alert if promote stalls > 90m.
eval-bot: after adjusting per-slice weight, re-run api_readme 30m shadow
eval-bot: api_readme (int8 weight=0.05) summary: halluc +0.006, embed_sim -0.015
nina: that's acceptable
sam: updating canary config and will kick a staggered live 0.2% for longform only, with per-slice int8 cap=0.2 and adaptive decay policy

```yaml
canary_id: v4-alpha-int8-cascade
stages:
  - name: shadow
    fraction: 0.10
    duration_mins: 90
  - name: narrow-live
    fraction: 0.002
    duration_mins: 60
  - name: ramp-1
    fraction: 0.01
    duration_mins: 60
  - name: broad
    fraction: 0.05
    duration_mins: 120
hysteresis:
  windows_required: 2
  window_mins: 30
gating:
  metrics: [rouge_delta, exact_match_delta, halluc_delta, latency_p95_delta, embed_sim_delta]
  pass_require: 4
  slice_abort_threshold: 0.06
advanced:
  per_slice_variant_cap: 0.2
  per_slice_decay: halve_on_first_breach
  min_variant_weight: 0.05
  safety_penalty: {halluc: 2.0}
alerts:
  latency_hard_cap: 0.2
  promote_stall_mins: 90
```

ops-sre: please ensure metrics emitted: per-variant kv_warmup_sec, per-slice sample_count, uplift_CI for rouge and exact_match, final_score timeseries
derek: suggestion: log example pairs where hallucation triggered for rapid eval by annotators (redwood-evals queue)
product-amy: i'll notify the owners of api_readme slice to monitor and pause if they see UX regressions
sam: timeline: push to staging tonight 0100 UTC, run shadow tomorrow 0900 UTC, if stable begin narrow-live after 2h manual thumbs-up else revert to pt-only
nina: thanks. small ask: include a short explainer in the rollout notes about why per-slice caps exist and how they prevent noisy global rollbacks
sam: will add that to the canary notes in console
eval-bot: shadow -> narrow-live attempted; narrow-live triggered auto-hysteresis window 1 pass, window 2 pass -> incremented to 0.01
eval-bot: final state after 6h: promoted to broad 0.05 with per-slice int8 cap applied; no active slice aborts; monitoring alerts fired for a transient p95 spike at T+2h resolved by autoscaling
ops-sre: postmortem note: transient spike correlated with autoscaler lag, increased scale buffer for future ramps
derek: good outcome; capturing lessons learned for runbook: prefer adaptive per-slice caps for quantized variants, always include targeted shadow runs for problematic slices
product-amy: :tada:
ops-sre: closing loop, will watch overnight and escalate if anything pops
